evidence: Cic. Off. 3.65: nisi nōminātim dictum esset
terms.comment: Nōminātim is “by name, one by one, expressly”, and goes with any verb of saying or naming: nōminātim excipere, to except by name (Cic. Att. 11.7.2).

terms.gloss: fix, set exactly (a time, a term, a limit)
terms.comment: To set bounds to, and so to fix; for its sense “define”, see define.

terms.gloss: lay down, prescribe (what is to be done)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.26.2: sīc enim praescrīpsimus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: id statuērunt, sī venditor scīret, nisi nōminātim dictum esset, praestārī oportēre.
phrases.english: they ruled that, if the seller knew of the defect, he must make it good, unless it had been expressly stated.

phrases.latin: ibi ego dīcam quidquid inerit nōminātim
phrases.english: I’ll tell you everything that’s in it, item by item

sources: Lewis & Short: nominatim · Lewis & Short: definio · Lewis & Short: praescribo
